evidence: Receiving DO2: 12.82 mg/L at 46.0 h, 5.85 mg/L at 46.2 h, 3.27 mg/L at 52.0 h — sustained ~0.5 mg/L/h decline toward the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving P assay (t=48 h, available 52 h): 2.92 g/L, comparable to source batches (~3.0 g/L) at same age — production on track, mass must be retained
Allowed action bounds: combined = feed x0.8, air x1.15 (vs increase_air alone or strong_feed_reduction x0.6)
Source batches show steep oxygen-demand ramp during this growth phase, with recovery only after feed/conditions change; receiving vessel shows worse DO2 supply-demand balance
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed from ~12.8 mg/L (46 h) to ~3.27 mg/L (52 h), declining ~0.5 mg/L/h — on track to violate the 2.0 mg/L minimum within hours. This is an oxygen supply/demand imbalance during the high-demand production phase, while product accumulation (2.92 g/L at 48 h) is healthy and must be retained. The combined intervention (feed x0.8, air x1.15) reduces oxygen demand 20% and raises transfer 15%, giving robust margin above the DO2 floor while sacrificing far less product mass than strong_feed_reduction (x0.6). KEEP alone risks violation; increase_air alone leaves thin margin if demand keeps rising; stop yields zero counted production.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving-vessel kinetic parameters and the true future oxygen-demand trajectory are unavailable; if demand is already peaking, increase_air alone might suffice and combined costs some titer, whereas continued demand growth could require further adjustment after this bounded action. Latest product assay is 4 h stale, so current product state is inferred from DO2 dynamics.
